paragraphs: Ben Bag Bag, Avot 5; Bekhorot 12a: Yochanan ben Bag Bag. When their teacher approved their statements, they wrote their then-names: ben Bag Bag, ben He He, ben Zakkai. Eduyot: Pappias and R.Y. [ר״י; referent unresolved] disagree with him. Kiddushin 10b; Jerusalem Ketubbot, Af Al Pi 4; Sifrei Korach, “The Lord spoke to Aaron.” Tosefta Ketubbot 5: Yochanan ben Bag Bag wrote to Rabbi Yehudah ben Beteira in Netzivin. In Heilprin’s account, an Israelite betrothed to a priest may not eat terumah. Beteira: “I know you are versed in Torah’s inner chambers.” Eruvin 27b: Yochanan would carry the clothes of anyone explaining babbakar according to Bag Bag to the bathhouse; Pesachim 96a. I heard he was ben He He himself (see there), but Maimonides counts two. Heilprin reads Tosafot, Chagigah 1, as referring to both men as children of converts, and stresses the plural. Avot 5 separately gives both sayings: apparently two. Bag Bag means son of a male convert, son of a female convert, Sefer Hamma'arikh. Maimonides puts him with Hillel and Shammai, before destruction; I do not know. Apparently impossible: he disputes with Pappias, who lived with Eliezer and Yehoshua after destruction; see there.
